office_macro_execution_blocked.title: Office Macro Execution Blocked
office_macro_execution_blocked.description: Whether Office VBA macros originating from the internet are blocked by policy (macro-block GPO / Defender ASR), so a phishing attachment cannot auto-execute a macro. Secure value: true. Fires when macros are enabled by default and a malicious attachment can run on open.

script_execution_constrained.title: Script Execution Constrained
script_execution_constrained.description: Whether script/command interpreter execution is constrained (PowerShell Constrained Language mode and AllSigned/RemoteSigned execution policy, signed-only scripts), cutting the phishing-to-execution path via PowerShell/VBA/shell. Secure value: true. Fires when interpreters can run arbitrary unsigned payloads.

application_allowlisting_enforced.title: Application Allowlisting Enforced
application_allowlisting_enforced.description: Whether application/script allowlisting is enforced (WDAC/AppLocker on Windows; Gatekeeper assessments on macOS) so only approved, signed binaries may execute, blocking unsigned/unknown phishing payloads. Secure value: true. Fires when any downloaded binary may run.

web_dns_content_filtering_enabled.title: Web/DNS Content Filtering Enabled
web_dns_content_filtering_enabled.description: Whether protective DNS plus web/email content filtering is active on the endpoint to block known-malicious domains and phishing-payload download/callback. Secure value: true. Fires when arbitrary domains are resolvable and no web/email filtering blocks the lure.

behavior_monitoring_enabled.title: EDR/AV Behavior Monitoring Enabled
behavior_monitoring_enabled.description: Whether EDR/AV behavior-based monitoring is active on the endpoint (Get-MpComputerStatus BehaviorMonitorEnabled True) so post-click payload execution and fileless/behavior-only malware are detected and blocked. Secure value: true. Fires when behavior monitoring is off and a payload executes undetected.

edr_av_present.title: Endpoint Anti-Malware (EDR/AV) Present
edr_av_present.description: Endpoint anti-malware (EDR/AV) is installed and its service is running (Get-MpComputerStatus AMServiceEnabled and AntivirusEnabled both True). When false, the core malware-defense control is absent and malware executes unimpeded.

realtime_protection_enabled.title: EDR/AV Real-Time Protection Enabled
realtime_protection_enabled.description: Real-time / on-access scanning is active (Get-MpComputerStatus RealTimeProtectionEnabled and OnAccessProtectionEnabled True) so files are inspected on access and boot/logon autostart persistence is observed. When false, files execute without on-access inspection, allowing malware to run and persistence to go unmonitored.

edr_tamper_protection_enabled.title: EDR/AV Tamper Protection Enabled
edr_tamper_protection_enabled.description: Tamper protection prevents malware or a local actor from disabling AV/EDR or altering its settings (Get-MpComputerStatus IsTamperProtected True). When false, an Impair-Defenses actor can silently disable the agent.

antivirus_signature_age_days.title: Anti-Malware Signature Age (days)
antivirus_signature_age_days.description: Age in days of the anti-malware signature/definition package (Get-MpComputerStatus AntivirusSignatureAge). Fires when above the freshness threshold (>3 days) because stale signatures miss known threats. Secure endpoints sit at or near 0.

removable_media_control_enabled.title: Removable-Media Device Control Enabled
removable_media_control_enabled.description: Removable-media device control restricts USB mass-storage write/execute via policy. When false, removable media can seed a malware payload (Replication Through Removable Media).

os_patch_current.title: OS and Client Software Patch-Current
os_patch_current.description: True when the OS and third-party client software (browser, document readers) have no missing critical/important security updates per the org patch SLA. Secure value is true; the exposure fires when patches are missing (false), leaving known-vulnerable client software exploitable via web or document content.

automatic_updates_enabled.title: Automatic Updates Enabled
automatic_updates_enabled.description: True when automatic OS and software updates are enabled so security fixes install without manual intervention within the SLA window. Secure value is true; the exposure fires when auto-update is disabled (false), since the endpoint drifts out of date and remains exploitable.

days_since_last_security_patch.title: Days Since Last Security Patch
days_since_last_security_patch.description: Number of days since the most recent security patch / cumulative update was installed (latest InstalledOn date via Get-HotFix or the equivalent). A hardened endpoint patches within SLA so this stays small (secure ~0); the exposure fires when it exceeds 30 days, indicating the patch SLA has lapsed.

credential_guard_enabled.title: Credential Guard Enabled
credential_guard_enabled.description: Windows Defender Credential Guard is running (Win32_DeviceGuard SecurityServicesRunning includes 1), isolating LSASS-derived secrets (NTLM hashes, Kerberos TGTs, cached domain credentials) in a VBS-protected container so they cannot be harvested from LSASS memory. Insecure (false) when off and LSASS secrets are harvestable for reuse.

lsa_protection_enabled.title: LSA Protection (RunAsPPL) Enabled
lsa_protection_enabled.description: LSA protection (RunAsPPL — LSASS runs as a Protected Process Light) is enabled, blocking unprivileged/userland tools from opening LSASS to dump credential material. Insecure (false) when LSASS is unprotected and credential-dumping tooling can read secrets directly.

endpoint_runs_as_least_privileged_user.title: Endpoint Runs as Least-Privileged User
endpoint_runs_as_least_privileged_user.description: Interactive day-to-day user accounts are standard users and the local Administrators group is limited to authorized admin accounts (least privilege, NIST AC-6). Insecure (false) when the everyday user holds local admin rights, granting the elevation needed to access LSASS, the SAM, and cached secrets for credential theft.

phishing_resistant_mfa_enabled.title: Phishing-Resistant MFA Enabled
phishing_resistant_mfa_enabled.description: Device/identity sign-in and resource access enforce phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2/WebAuthn, Windows Hello for Business, or certificate) rather than password-only or phishable OTP/push. Insecure (false) when password-only/phishable auth is used, so stolen endpoint credentials can be replayed to move laterally.

endpoint_full_disk_encryption_on.title: Full-Disk Encryption On
endpoint_full_disk_encryption_on.description: Full-disk encryption is on and complete for the system volume (BitLocker: VolumeStatus=FullyEncrypted, ProtectionStatus=On, EncryptionPercentage=100; FileVault: 'FileVault is On.'). Secure value is true; an unencrypted disk or suspended protector leaves local data and cached credentials readable to an offline attacker who physically possesses a lost or stolen device.

tpm_present_and_ready.title: TPM Present and Ready
tpm_present_and_ready.description: A TPM is present and ready (TpmPresent=True and TpmReady=True via Get-Tpm, TPM 2.0 expected) to anchor boot/credential integrity and the disk-encryption key. Without a hardware-anchored key protector, the encryption key is more readily extractable offline and boot integrity is not hardware-anchored. Fires when no ready TPM is available.

screen_lock_timeout_minutes.title: Screen-Lock Inactivity Timeout (minutes)
screen_lock_timeout_minutes.description: Inactivity timeout in minutes after which the device automatically locks and requires a password/biometric to wake. Secure value is a short timeout (<= 15 minutes); a long or absent timeout widens the window during which a lost or unattended device exposes an unlocked, decrypted session. The exposure fires when the timeout exceeds 15 minutes.

remote_wipe_enabled.title: Remote Wipe Capability Enabled
remote_wipe_enabled.description: The organization can remotely lock/wipe this endpoint via MDM/UEM (an available, tested Wipe/Retire/Lock action in the MDM console). Secure value is true; without remote-wipe capability a lost or stolen device cannot be remediated, prolonging exposure of local data and cached credentials. Grounded in NIST SP 800-124 Rev. 2.

secure_boot_enabled.title: UEFI Secure Boot Enabled
secure_boot_enabled.description: UEFI Secure Boot is enabled so only signed bootloaders/firmware run, preventing boot-level persistence and bootkits. Verified via Confirm-SecureBootUEFI (True = enabled/secure; False = supported-but-disabled/insecure). Fires when Secure Boot is disabled, leaving the boot chain open to unsigned/tampered boot components.

managed_device_enrollment_enforced.title: Managed Device Enrollment Enforced
managed_device_enrollment_enforced.description: The endpoint is enrolled and compliant in the org MDM/UEM (Intune/Jamf) so policy, patch, and configuration are centrally enforced and remote wipe is possible. True = managed (secure); False = unenrolled/unmanaged/non-compliant (insecure — the device escapes central control).

endpoint_audit_logs_centralised.title: Endpoint Logs Forwarded to Central SIEM/EDR
endpoint_audit_logs_centralised.description: Endpoint security/EDR alerts and OS security logs are forwarded to a central SIEM/EDR cloud so detections and incident evidence survive a compromised host. True = telemetry shipped centrally (secure); False = logs local-only or forwarding broken (insecure — a compromise goes undetected).

host_firewall_enabled.title: Host Firewall Enabled on All Profiles
host_firewall_enabled.description: The host-based firewall is enabled on ALL profiles (Domain/Private/Public) to limit inbound exposure and lateral movement. True = enabled on every profile (secure); False = any profile disabled (insecure — inbound exposure / lateral-movement surface).

vpn_ztna_posture_gating_enabled.title: VPN/ZTNA Posture Gating Enabled
vpn_ztna_posture_gating_enabled.description: Off-network access to corporate systems is enforced through VPN/ZTNA with device-compliance/posture gating rather than direct internet exposure. True = VPN/ZTNA required with posture check (secure); False = direct internet exposure / no posture check (insecure — off-network exposure).
